purpose: Executable ledger for the `semantic-ontology-language` route-support family; normalized schema envelope added in rev0293.
non_promotion_rule: Semantic-term rows define controlled meanings and equivocation tests. They can cap, freeze, or roll back wording; they cannot promote a route or create evidence.

semantic_rows.preferred_meaning: “reconstruction” means a code-subspace / dictionary-relative reconstruction up to declared gauge, frame, finite-N, and quotient limitations; it does not mean global bulk ontology identity.
prohibited_equivocations: equating presentation equivalence with ontology identity
treating an operational record label as a native theoretical term
using familiar public-theory vocabulary as if it were candidate-native
letting a synonym, acronym, or generated summary alter authority
semantic_rows.observational_bridge_terms: public-record terms remain bridge terms until carrier, acquisition, measurement, and semantic rows bind them to the route target grain
semantic_rows.theory_internal_terms: candidate-native terms are allowed only inside the declared route quotient, domain, and state-machine ceiling
semantic_rows.semantic_stability_test: rewrite the claim using only controlled terms, then check whether route state, target grain, contrast class, and rollback handle remain unchanged under synonyms, dual presentation, and public-vs-native vocabulary swaps

semantic_rows.preferred_meaning: metadata and generated summaries are custody, indexing, and replay aids; they are not physical evidence, semantic closure, ontology commitment, or route promotion.
prohibited_equivocations: treating a clean package as confirmation
treating a generated mirror as a new record
treating a release slug as a scientific claim
treating provenance as ontology
semantic_rows.observational_bridge_terms: metadata can point to public carriers but cannot create one
semantic_rows.theory_internal_terms: metadata has no candidate-native theoretical vocabulary unless a route-specific row imports it under declared limits
semantic_rows.semantic_stability_test: remove the metadata wrapper and check whether the physical or formal support sentence still holds; if not, the sentence was custody-only
